documents.title: Artificial Intelligence
documents.text:
Artificial Intelligence
The tools available in Dragonfly for implementing powerful artificial intelligence solutions for the segmentation of multi-dimensional images include the Segmentation Wizard, Machine Learning Segmentation, and the Deep Learning Tool. In addition, deep learning architectures for object detection and noise-to-void denoising are implemented in the Custom Deep Model Architectures module. Options for applying trained regression models are available in the Filter with AI panel, while options for applying semantic segmentation models are available in the Segment with AI panel.
In This Section
Segmentation Wizard
Machine Learning Segmentation
Deep Learning Tool
Custom Deep Model Architectures
Filter with AI
Segment with AI

documents.path: Artificial Intelligence/Custom Deep Model Architectures/Classification/Applying Classification Models.htm
documents.title: Applying Classification Models
documents.text:
Applying Classification Models
Classification model outputs range from the classification of object instances to confidence and probabilities maps. Models, inputs and outputs, as well as output types, can be selected on the Apply tab of the Classification dialog, as shown below.
Apply tab
An example of an input dataset, output multi-ROI, and classification of labeled instances is shown below.
Input dataset (left), output multi-ROI with labeled instances (center), classified multi-ROI in which defective solder balls are highlighted in red (right)
You should note that the current implementation of classification is strictly 2D, which means that training and inference will be done on a slice-by-slice basis in the Z-axis.
The following options are available for applying trained classification models on the Apply tab in the Classification dialog (see Apply Tab).
Apply options
Description
Model
Lets you choose the required model.
Note See Model Box for additional information about filtering and other options for listed models.
Parameters
Lets you choose the input dataset and output multi-ROI.
Input… Lets you choose the dataset that the model will use to extract image features for classification.
Output… Lets you choose an output multi-ROI, which must include the segmented object instances that correspond to the selected input.
Output type
You can choose an output type — Segmentation or Probabilities — in the Output Type box, shown below.
Segmentation… If selected, object instances will be classified in a new multi-ROI as per the model's training.
Probabilities… If selected, scalar values of the confidence or probability of the model's predictions will be added to a new multi-ROI.
Confidence maps represent the model's estimated confidence that an instance is classified correctly, while probability maps represent the model's estimated probability that an instance is classified correctly. Probability maps are closely related to confidence maps, but with a stronger emphasis on normalized probabilities rather than arbitrary confidence scores. You can compute probabilities for all classes or for a selected class.
Note Probabilities can play a crucial role in deep learning by helping to quantify uncertainty in model predictions. This can be especially important in cases in which understanding the confidence and/or probabilities of a model’s predictions can significantly impact decision making.
Apply
Lets you choose the extent to which the selected model will be applied.
Full Dataset… The full dataset will be processed.
Marked Slices… Only marked slices will be processed (see Marking Slices and Modifying Image Stacks).
With ROI as Mask… Only data that intersects with the labeled voxels within the selected region of interest will be processed (see Creating Mask ROIs).
With Shape as Mask… Only data that intersects with the selected shape will be processed (see Shapes Panel).
How to Apply a Classification Model
Choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architecture > Classification on the menu bar.
The Classification dialog appears.
Select the required model on the Apply tab.
Note You can filter the model list by entering key words in the Filter edit box, if required.
Choose an input dataset and output multi-ROI in the Parameters box, as shown below.
Expand the Output Type box, if required, and then choose an output type.
Note Refer to the table Apply options for information about output types.
Click the Apply button and then choose how you want to apply the model, as shown below.
Note If chose to apply the model with a mask, you will need to choose a mask in the Choose an ROI as Mask dialog, as shown below, or in the Choose a Shape as Mask dialog.
The selected model is loaded and then applied. When processing is complete, a new multi-ROI appears in the Data Properties and Settings panel.

documents.title: Classification Interface
documents.text:
Classification Interface
The Classification dialog contains of a number of tabs and panels — Apply and Train — that you let you configure and complete a model training workflow, as well as apply a trained classification model to selected datasets.
You should note that the current implementation of classification is strictly 2D, which means that training and inference will be done on a slice-by-slice basis in the Z-axis.
Choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architectures > Classification on the menu bar to open the Classification dialog, shown below.
Classification dialog
Typical outputs for classification models are multi-ROIs with defined classes for the segmented object instances. You should note that the task of classifying instances in multi-ROIs can be accelerated with Dragonfly’s Instance Labeler tool (see Instance Labeler).
Apply Tab
You can apply a trained model to classify objects on a selected dataset on the Apply tab, shown below.
A. Model box B. Parameters box C. Output Type box D. Apply
Model Box
The following options are available in the Model box on the Apply tab:
You can filter the models in the list by entering keywords in the Filter edit box.
You can right-click a model and then choose Open Model Folder in File Browser to open the model folder.
You can right click a model and then choose Display Training Metrics to view the training results of any training session.
Parameters Box
The options available in the Parameters box, shown below, let you choose an input image channel and an output multi-ROI with the segmented object instances.
Parameters box
Refer to the topic Applying Classification Models for information about applying a trained model to classify objects in a selected dataset.
Output Type Box
The options available in the Output Type box, shown below, let you choose an output type — the classification results for the segmentation or the probabilities map for the classification results.
Output Type Box
Refer to the topic Applying Classification Models for more information about the output types.
Apply
Once the input and output selections are done, the selected model can be applied on the full dataset, marked slices, or with a region of interest or shape as a mask. Refer to the topic Applying Classification Models for information about applying a trained model to classify objects in a selected dataset.
Train Panel
The tabs on the Train panel — Models, Inputs, and Training Parameters — provide the controls and settings that let you generate and train models for object classification (see Training Classification Models). You should note that most of the functionalities such as input options, data augmentation, and training parameters, are the same as those for the Deep Learning Tool.
Tabs on the Train panel
Each tab on the Train panel includes an estimate of memory needed to train the model, as well as options to generate a one-slice preview of a selected model's inference (see Generating Previews) and to initiate training (see Training Classification Models).
Estimated Memory Ratio
Each tab on the Train panel displays an estimated memory ratio, which is calculated as the ratio of your system's capability and the estimated memory needed to train the model at the current over the available GPU memory. You should note that the memory needed to train a deep model is dependent on the depth of the model, as well as the selected patch and/or batch sizes.
Green … The estimated memory requirements are within your system's capabilities, typically less than 0.90.
Yellow … The estimated memory requirements are approaching your system's capabilities. Ratios between 0.90 and 1.00 may or may not result in successful training. You can adjust the batch and/or patch size to reduce the estimated memory requirement.
Red … The estimated memory requirements exceed your system's capabilities. Training often fails when ratios are greater than 1.0. You should consider adjusting the model training parameters, such as the batch and/or patch size, or selecting a shallower model, if possible.
Models Tab
The Models tab, shown below, includes controls to create new models, as well as to set the visibility and highlight colors of the labeled classes.
A. Model box B. Classes box
Model Box
You can create new models in the Model box on the Models tab, as well as duplicate and delete models.
Model box
The following options are available in the Model box on the Models tab on the Train panel:
Model settings and controls
Description
Filter
Lets you filter the model list by Model Name key words. You can also sort the list in ascending or descending order.
Model Name and Date
Indicates the name assigned to models, as well as the data and time that they were create.
Note You can edit the name of a model by double-clicking, as well right-click to open the folder in which the model was saved and to view its training history.
New
Lets you create a new model for object detection (see Generating New YOLOv7 Models).
Duplicate
Creates a copy of the selected model.
Note The name of a duplicated model can be edited by double-clicking it in the Model Name column.
Delete
Deletes the selected model.
Classes Box
The items in the Classes box correspond to the number of classes selected in the Model Information dialog when the selected model was generated. You can rename the classes, apply new colors, and choose to show or hide any of the classes when creating previews.
Classes box
Inputs Tab
The Inputs tab on the Train panel, shown below, includes an Inputs box for choosing training sets and data augmentation settings for generating addition training data.
A. Inputs box B. Data augmentation settings
Inputs Box
You can choose the input(s), output, and mask for defining the model's working space in the Inputs box, shown below.
Inputs box
The following settings and options are available in the Inputs box.
Inputs box settings and options
Description
Dataset list
-
Lists all of the training sets selected for model training. Items include the following:
Input… Lets you select the input image(s) for training the model. You can choose multiple inputs for the training input. For example, when you are working with color images.
Output… Lets you select a target output for training, which must be a multi-ROI (see Training Prerequisites).
Mask… Lets you select a mask to define the working space for the model, which can help reduce training times and increase training accuracy. You should note that masks should be large enough to enclose the selected Patch size and that rectangular shapes are often best (see Applying Masks).
The starting point of the input (patch) grid is calculated from the minimum (0,0) of each connected component in the mask. You should note input (patches) that do not correspond 100% with the applied mask will be ignored during training. You should also note that patches that correspond to the applied mask, but that are not fully segmented, will be ignored during training. For example, in cases in which the background (class 1) is not labeled.
Edit Calibration
Opens the Normalization dialog, in which you can normalize calibrated and uncalibrated datasets prior to training (see Normalizing Data Ranges Prior to Training or Inference).
Show Statistics
Opens the Training Data Statistics dialog, shown below. The dialog lists the total number of voxels in the training set(s), the total number of labeled training voxels used and its percentage of the total number of voxels in the training set(s), as well as the number of training voxels used by each specified class label and their percentage of the total number of voxels used. You should note that all statistics are computed within selected masks.
Add
Adds a new item to the datasets list. The input(s) can be selected in their respective drop-down menus.
Remove
Removes the selected item from the datasets list.
Export as AI
Saves all training data inputs, outputs, and masks as slices in the native Dragonfly (*.ORSObject extension) file format. Saving only data that is used for training can significantly reduce the size of training sets.
Import as AI
Imports all training data that was exported as AI. All saved inputs, outputs, and masks for each training set will be added to the dialog when the data is imported, minimizing any additional manual entry.
Inspect Patches
Patch size can be a critical factor when training classification models and must be selected in consideration of the specific characteristics of the input data, the model architecture, and the typical size of the labeled object instances.
Click the Inspect Patches button to review patches. Patches will be extracted based on the current patch size, data augmentation settings, and the selected input count. In the Patches Review dialog, shown below, you can review training and validation patches, visually inspect each patch, and extract additional information about all patches.
Patches Review dialog
Data Augmentation Settings
The performance of neural networks often improves with the amount of data available, particularly the ability of the fit models to generalize what they have learned to new images.
You should consider experimenting with the different data augmentation methods to determine which ones result in a measurable improvement to model performance.
Check the Generate additional training data by augmentation option to activate the Data augmentation settings, shown below.
Data augmentation settings
Refer to the topic Data Augmentation Settings for more information about the Data augmentation settings.
Training Parameters Tab
The basic settings that you need to set to train a classification model are available in the Training parameters box, as shown below, on the Training Parameters tab.
A. Training parameters box B. Callbacks box C. Learning Rate Scheduler box
Training Parameters Box
The training parameters, shown and described below, are a stripped down version of those found in the Deep Learning Tool.
Training parameters box
Whenever you adjust the default training parameters, you should monitor the estimated memory ratio (see Estimated Memory Ratio) and make sure that your settings do not exceed your system's memory. You should also note that the default values should provide good results in most cases.
You can set the following parameters for training classification models.
Training parameters
Description
Patch size
Determines the size of the data patches that will be extracted from the training data and used as the input for training.
Important The selected patch size should correspond to the typical size of the object instances as much as possible. For example, you should choose a patch size of 64 if the typical object size is 64 x 64 pixels. In many cases, it is best to verify the selected size by inspecting the patches with the .
Batch size
Determines the number of patches in a batch, which are randomly processed during training. The model parameters will be updated whenever all of the patches in a batch have been processed.
Epochs number
Determines the maximum number of batches that will be processed.
Optimization algorithm
Lets you choose an optimization algorithm, which are used to update the model parameters so that the loss function is minimized. Optimization is a procedure in which the gradient — the partial derivative of the loss function with respect to the network's parameters — is first computed and then the model weights are modified by a given step size in the direction opposite of the gradient until a local minimum is achieved.
See Optimization Algorithms for additional information about the available optimization algorithms.
Learning rate
Determines the initial learning rate of the selected optimization algorithm.
Note The Learning Rate Scheduler can be set to dynamically adjust the learning rate of the selected optimization algorithm to help accelerate convergence.
Weight decay
Determines the initial weight decay of the selected optimization algorithm.
Callbacks Box
Callbacks are functions called during the training process, usually at the end of a training epoch or at the end of batch processing, that help optimize the training process. The 'Early stopping' callback, as shown below, is supported for training classification models.
Callbacks box
Although callbacks are often beneficial, they might cause undesired consequences when used improperly. For example, Early stopping might stop a training process too early, while a better solution could have been found if the training process would have been allowed to continue.
Early Stopping
The Early Stopping callback can be set to stop training when a monitored quantity reaches a specific value, or if the results do not improve after a specific number of epochs. This can help prevent overfitting. A good guideline when using early stopping is to choose a patience level that is coherent with the selected number of epochs.
You should note the following whenever you edit the 'Set patience' setting:
With the 'As a fixed value' option checked, the computation section will be disabled and the behavior will be 'normal' and the 'patience' value in the table will be applied
With the 'Using the following computation' option checked, the 'patience' value in table will not be editable, but will be updated with the calculation result.
Early stopping parameters
Description
monitor
Lets you choose the quantity to be monitored, for example, val_loss or loss.
patience
Is the number of epochs with no improvement after which training will be stopped.
min_delta
Is the minimum change in the monitored quantity to qualify as an improvement. An absolute change of less than min_delta, will count as no improvement.
baseline
Is the baseline value for the monitored quantity to reach. Training will stop if the model doesn't show improvement over the baseline.
Learning Rate Scheduler Box
The learning rate scheduler, shown below, can be set to dynamically adjust the learning rate of a selected optimizer to help accelerate convergence during the training process. Instead of using a fixed learning rate throughout training, which can lead to suboptimal convergence or slow training, schedulers modify the learning rate based on predefined rules or the model's performance.
Learning rate scheduler box
Refer to the topic Learning Rate Scheduler for information about selecting a learning rate scheduler and setting its parameters.

documents.path: Artificial Intelligence/Custom Deep Model Architectures/Classification/Image Clasification.htm
documents.title: Image Classification
documents.text:
Image Classification
Image classification is one of the most promising applications of deep learning to deliver the capability to recognize and classify the content of an image for anomaly detection and other automated visual inspection tasks.
In Dragonfly 3D World, the EfficientNetV2 family of image classification models is used as the feature extractor for classification tasks.
In This Section
Classification Interface
Training Classification Models
Applying Classification Models

documents.path: Artificial Intelligence/Custom Deep Model Architectures/Classification/Training Classification Models.htm
documents.title: Training Classification Models
documents.text:
Training Classification Models
Dragonfly's implementation of the EfficientNetV2 family of image classification models is accessible from the menu item Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architecture > Classification. This feature, which , which uses a combination of training-aware neural architecture search and scaling to optimize training speed and parameter efficiency, simplifies the training process and lets you apply trained models on selected datasets. The results of applying trained models is that each labeled object instance is classified, as shown below.
Input dataset (left), output multi-ROI with labeled instances (center), classified multi-ROI in which defective solder balls are highlighted in red (right)
You should note that the current implementation of classification is strictly 2D, which means that training and inference will be done on a slice-by-slice basis in the Z-axis.
About EfficientNetV2 Models
EfficientNetV2 are the family of image classification models used as the feature extractor for classification tasks. Built upon EfficientNetV1, EfficientNetV2 models use neural architecture search (NAS) to jointly optimize model size and training speed, and are scaled up in a way for faster training and inference speed. Refer to the documentation publications below, as well as the source code, for additional information about EfficientNetV2.
EfficientNetV2 — Torchvision main documentation: https://docs.pytorch.org/vision/main/models/efficientnetv2.html.
Publication: Mingxing Tan, Quoc V. Le, 2021. EfficientNetV2: Smaller Models and Faster Training, arXiv:2104.00298 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.00298).
Source code: https://github.com/pytorch/vision/blob/main/torchvision/models/efficientnet.py.
Training Prerequisites
The following items are required for training classification models:
Training dataset(s) for the input. See Cropping Datasets for information about extracting a training dataset as a subset of the original data.
A target for the output, which must be a multi-ROI.
Note The multi-ROI must have the same geometry as the input training dataset(s) and object instances must be labeled with a distinct class. You can use the Instance Labeler to prepare multi-ROIs as the output for training (see Instance Labeler).
The following items are optional for training classification models:
An ROI mask(s), for defining the working space for the model. For example, if you want to exclude some labeled areas from the training, then you would need a mask.
Note Refer to the topic Creating Mask ROIs for information about creating mask ROIs.
Generating Classification Models
Class count, input count, backbone, and dropout rate can be selected in the Model Information dialog whenever you generate new classification models.
Click the New button on the Train tab to open the Model Information dialog, shown below.
Model Information dialog
The following parameters can be set in the Model Information dialog for generating classification models.
Model parameters
Description
Model name
Lets you enter a name for the generated model.
Description
Lets you enter a description of your model.
Class count
Lets you enter the number of classes for training, which must be equal to the number of labeled classes in the output multi-ROI. For example, a classification model for anomaly detection in manufacturing often has two classes — 'Defective' and 'Non-defective'.
Input count
Lets you enter the number of inputs required for training. Additional inputs can be added whenever you are work with data from simultaneous image acquisition systems or want include filtered images in your training set.
You should note that all inputs must be registered and have the same geometry and shape.
Note Additional inputs can also be selected when you set the inputs on the Inputs tab (see Inputs Box).
Backbone
Lets you instantiate an EfficientNetV2 model with the backbones shown below.
EfficientNetV2S… Constructs an EfficientNetV2S architecture from EfficientNetV2: Smaller Models and Faster Training (see also https://docs.pytorch.org/vision/main/models/generated/torchvision.models.efficientnet_v2_s.html#torchvision.models.efficientnet_v2_s).
EfficientNetV2M… Constructs an EfficientNetV2M architecture from EfficientNetV2: Smaller Models and Faster Training (see also https://docs.pytorch.org/vision/main/models/generated/torchvision.models.efficientnet_v2_m.html#torchvision.models.efficientnet_v2_m).
EfficientNetV2L… Constructs an EfficientNetV2L architecture from EfficientNetV2: Smaller Models and Faster Training (see also https://docs.pytorch.org/vision/main/models/generated/torchvision.models.efficientnet_v2_l.html#torchvision.models.efficientnet_v2_l).
Dropout rate
Lets you choose a dropout rate. Dropout is often used in training to minimize overfitting and improve classification and prediction accuracy. It operates by randomly zeroing some of the elements of the input tensor with a given probability.
How to Generate a Classification Model
Choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architectures > Classification on the menu bar.
The Classification dialog appears.
Click the New button on the Train tab.
The Model Information dialog appears.
Enter a name and description for the new model, as required.
Choose the required Class count, as shown below.
Note The entered Class count must be equal to the number of labeled classes in the output multi-ROI.
Choose an Input count, as required.
Set the model hyperparameters 'Backbone' and 'Dropout rate'.
Note Refer to the table above for information about the available hyperparameters.
Click OK.
After processing is complete, the model appears in the Model list and the selected number of classes appears in the Classes box.
Continue to the topic Training Classification Models to learn how to train your new model.
Training Classification Models
You can start training an EfficientNetV2 model for image classification after you have prepared your training input(s) and output, as well as any required masks (see Training Prerequisites).
The initial set of training parameters should work well in most cases. You should also note that the training parameters and weights are saved with each model and can be reused for future training.
How to Train a Classification Model
Open the Classification dialog, if it is not already onscreen.
To open the dialog, choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architecture > Classification on the menu bar.
Do one of the following, as required:
Generate a new model for object detection (see Generating Classification Models).
Select an untrained or trained model from the Model list on the Models tab that contains the required number of inputs and output classes.
Do the following in the Inputs box on the Inputs tab for each training set you want to train the model with:
Choose your input(s) in the Input drop-down menu(s).
Note You can also click the Add New button and then choose an additional input for training.
Choose the multi-ROI labeled for classification in the Output drop-down menu.
Note Only multi-ROIs with the number of classes corresponding to model's class count and that have the same geometry as the input dataset will be available in the menu.
Choose a mask in the Mask drop-down menu, optional.
The completed Inputs for a single training set with one input should look something like this:
The completed Inputs for a single training set with multiple inputs should look something like this:
The completed Inputs for multiple training sets should look something like this:
Note In all cases, you click the Inspect Patches button to evaluate the training and validation patches (see Inspect Patches).
Adjust the Data augmentation settings, as required (see Data Augmentation Settings).
Adjust the Training parameters on the Training Parameters tab, as required (see Training Parameters Tab).
Note You should monitor the estimated memory ratio when you choose the training parameter settings. The ratio should not exceed 0.90 (see Estimated Memory Ratio).
Click the Train button.
The dataset is validated and then automatically split into training and validation sets before training begins. You can monitor the progress of training in the Training Model dialog, as shown below.
During training, the quantities 'loss' and 'validation loss' should decrease.
Note You can also click the List tab and then view the training metric values for each epoch.
Wait for training to be completed. You can also stop training at anytime, if required.
Evaluate the results for the training session, recommended (see Evaluating Training Results).
Generate previews to evaluate the model, recommended (see Generating Previews).
If the results are not satisfactory, you should consider doing one or more of the following and then retraining the model:
Add an additional training set.
Create a mask centered on problematic areas (see Creating Mask ROIs).
Remove or adjust the data augmentation settings (see Data Augmentation Settings).
Adjust the training parameter settings (see Training Parameters Tab).
Apply the model to the original dataset or to similar datasets (see Applying Classification Models), as required.
Generating Previews
You can generate one-slice previews of a trained model's inference with the options in the Preview box, which is available on all tabs of the Train panel.
Preview box
How to Generate a Preview
Select the required model on the Models tab, if not already done.
Note You can show or hide a class by default by changing the visibility of a class in the Classes box on the Models tab, optional.
Make sure that the input image is visible in the workspace views, recommended.
Select the required input image(s) in the Input drop-down menu.
Select the required output multi-ROI.
Note The output multi-ROI must include the segmented object instances that you want to classify and must have the same geometry as the input image(s).
Click the Apply button.
The preview appears in the workspace views.

documents.text:
Custom Deep Model Architectures
Dragonfly's Custom Deep Model Architectures module supports deep models that have a different architecture than the ones supported in the Deep Learning Tool. The current models implemented in the module include Noise2Void for denoising and YOLOv7 for object detection.
In This Section
Image Classification
Denoising with Noise2Void
Object Detection with YOLOv7

documents.path: Artificial Intelligence/Custom Deep Model Architectures/Denoising with Noise2Void/Applying Noise2Void Models.htm
documents.title: Applying Noise2Void Models
documents.text:
Applying Noise2Void Models
You can automatically denoise datasets with any of the Noise2Void models that you trained (seeTraining Noise2Void Models for information about training a Noise2Void model).
The following options are available for applying trained Noise2Void models on the Apply tab in the Noise2Void dialog.
Apply options
Description
Model
Lets you choose the required model (see Model Box for additional information about filtering and other options for listed models).
Parameters
Lets you choose the input dataset.
Apply
Lets you choose how to apply the selected model to the input dataset. The resulting multi-ROI will added to the Data Properties and Settings panel when processing is complete.
Full Dataset… If selected, the full dataset will be denoised.
With Mask… If selected, only data within the region of interest selected as the mask will be processed.
How to Apply a Noise2Void Model
Choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architectures > Noise2Void on the menu bar.
The Noise2Void dialog appears.
Filter the model list on the Apply tab by entering key words in the Filter edit box, if required.
Select the model that you want to use.
The items in the Parameters box are activated.
Choose the dataset that you want to apply the model to in the Input drop-down menu.
Click the Apply button and then choose how you want to apply the model — to the Full Dataset or With Mask.
Note If chose to apply the model with a mask, you will need to choose a mask in the Choose a Mask ROI dialog, as shown below.
The selected model is loaded and then applied. When processing is complete, a new dataset of the inference appears in the Data Properties and Settings panel.

documents.path: Artificial Intelligence/Custom Deep Model Architectures/Denoising with Noise2Void/Denoising with Noise2Void.htm
documents.title: Denoising with Noise2Void
documents.text:
Denoising with Noise2Void
Training deep-learning models for denoising usually relies on either pairing high-noise input images with low-noise output images or using independent pairs of noisy images in an approach known as Noise2Noise (N2N). These approaches can be limited if the acquisition of low-noise or noisy training targets is not possible, as is often the case for biomedical image studies. As an alternative, an approach known as Noise2Void (N2V), in which training is done directly on the data to be denoised, is available option for training deep models for denoising .
In This Section
Noise2Void Interface
Training Noise2Void Models
Applying Noise2Void Models

documents.path: Artificial Intelligence/Custom Deep Model Architectures/Denoising with Noise2Void/Noise2Void Interface.htm
documents.title: Noise2Void Interface
documents.text:
Noise2Void Interface
The Noise2Void dialog contains of a number of tabs and panels — Apply and Train — that let you configure and complete a model training workflow, as well as apply a trained model to denoise a dataset.
Choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architectures > Noise2Void on the menu bar to open the Noise2Void dialog, shown below.
Noise2Void dialog
Apply Tab
You can apply a trained denoising model to a selected dataset on the Apply tab, shown below.
A. Model box B. Parameters box C. Apply
Model Box
The following options are available in the Model box on the Apply tab:
You can filter the models in the list by entering keywords in the Filter edit box.
You can right-click a model and then choose Open Model Folder in File Browser to open the model folder.
You can right click a model and then choose Display Training Metrics to view the training results of any training session, as shown below.
Parameters Box
The Input option available in the Parameters box lets you choose the dataset that will be denoised with the selected model.
Apply
Once the input selection is done, the model can be applied on the full dataset, marked slices, or within a mask. Refer to the topic Applying Noise2Void Models for information about applying a trained model to denoise datasets.
Train Panel
The tabs on the Train panel — Model, Inputs, and Training Parameters — provide the controls and settings that let you generate and train N2V models for denoising (see Training Noise2Void Models). You should note that most of the functionalities, such as input options, data augmentation, and training parameters, are the same as those for the Deep Learning Tool.
Tabs on the Train panel
Each tab on the Train panel includes an estimate of memory needed to train the model, as well as options to generate a one-slice preview of a selected model's inference (see Previewing Training Results) and to initiate training (see Training Noise2Void Models).
Estimated Memory Ratio
Each tab on the Train panel displays an estimated memory ratio, which is calculated as the ratio of your system's capability and the estimated memory needed to train the model at the current over the available GPU memory. You should note that the memory needed to train a deep model is dependent on the depth of the model, as well as the selected patch and/or batch sizes.
Green … The estimated memory requirements are within your system's capabilities, typically less than 0.90.
Yellow … The estimated memory requirements are approaching your system's capabilities. Ratios between 0.90 and 1.00 may or may not result in successful training. You can adjust the batch and/or patch size to reduce the estimated memory requirement.
Red … The estimated memory requirements exceed your system's capabilities. Training often fails when ratios are greater than 1.0. You should consider adjusting the model training parameters, such as the batch and/or patch size, or selecting a shallower model, if possible.
Models Tab
All available Noise2Void models are listed in the top section of the Models tab in the Train panel. You can generate new models, duplicate and delete models, as well open the model folder and display the training history, in the Model box.
Model box
The following settings and options are available in the Model box.
Settings and options for models
Description
Filter
Lets you filter the model list by Model Name key words. You can also sort the list in ascending or descending order.
Model list
Model Name
Indicates the name assigned to the model. You can edit the name of a model by double-clicking.
Date
Indicates the date and time that the model was created.
Pop-up menu
You can right-click a model and then open the model folder or view the training results of any training session, as shown in the screenshot above.
Model controls
New
Lets you create a new Noise2Void model (see Generating Noise2Void Models).
Duplicate
Creates a copy of the selected model.
Note The name of a duplicated model can be edited by double-clicking it in the Model Name column.
Delete
Deletes the selected model.
Inputs Tab
The Inputs tab, shown below, includes an Inputs box for choosing training sets, data augmentation settings for generating addition training data, and the settings for visual feedback.
A. Inputs box B. Data augmentation settings C. Visual feedback settings
Inputs Box
You can choose the input(s), output(s), and mask(s) for defining the model working space in the Inputs box, shown below.
Inputs box
The following settings and options are available in the Inputs box.
Inputs box settings and options
Icon
Description
Inputs list
-
Lists all of the training sets selected for model training.
Items include the following:
Input… Lets you select the input(s) for training the model. You can choose multiple inputs for the training input. For example, when you are working with color images.
Mask… Lets you select a mask to define the working space for the model, which can help reduce training times and increase training accuracy. You should note that masks should be large enough to enclose the selected Patch size and that rectangular shapes are often best (see Applying Masks).
Edit Calibration
Opens the Normalization dialog, in which you can normalize calibrated and uncalibrated datasets prior to training (see Normalizing Data Ranges Prior to Training or Inference).
Add
Adds a new item to the datasets list. The input(s) for the item can be selected in the respective drop-down menus.
Remove
Removes the selected item from the datasets list.
Export as AI
Saves all training data inputs and masks as slices in the native Dragonfly (*.ORSObject extension) file format. Saving only data that is used for training can significantly reduce the size of training sets.
Import as AI
Imports all training data that was exported as AI. All saved inputs, outputs, and masks for each training set will be added to the dialog when the data is imported, minimizing any additional manual entry.
Data Augmentation Settings
A common way to compensate small training sets is to use data augmentation. If selected, different transformations will be applied to simulate more data than is actually available. Images may be flipped vertically or horizontally, rotated, sheared, or scaled. As such, specific data augmentation options should be chosen within the context of the training dataset and knowledge of the problem domain. In addition, you should consider experimenting with the different data augmentation methods to determine which ones result in a measurable improvement to model performance, perhaps with a small dataset, model, and training run.
Note Although the performance of neural networks often improves with data augmentation, this might not be the case when training Noise2Void models.
Check the Generate additional training data by augmentation option to activate the Data augmentation settings, shown below.
Data augmentation settings
Refer to the topic Data Augmentation Settings for more information about the Data augmentation settings.
Visual Feedback Settings
To help monitor and evaluate the progress of training Noise2Void models, you can designate a 2D rectangular region for visual feedback (see Enabling Visual Feedback). With the Visual Feedback option selected, the model’s inference will be displayed in the Training dialog in real time as each epoch is completed, as shown on the screen capture below.
Training dialog
In addition, you can create a checkpoint cache so that you can save a copy of the model at a selected checkpoint (see Saving and Loading Model Checkpoints). Saved checkpoints are marked in bold on the plotted graph.
Training Parameters Tab
The training parameters that you need to set to train a Noise2Void model are available on the Training Parameters tab, as shown below.
A. Training parameters box B. Callbacks box C. Learning Rate Scheduler box
Training Parameters Box
The training parameters, shown and described below, are a stripped down version of those found in the Deep Learning Tool.
Training parameters box
You can set the following parameters for training Noise2Void models.
Whenever you adjust the default training parameters, you should monitor the estimated memory ratio (see Estimated Memory Ratio) and make sure that your settings do not exceed your system's memory. You should also note that the default values should provide good results in most cases.
Training parameters
Description
Pixel ratio (%)
Is the percentage to pixels that will be manipulated per patch.
Note In most cases, a pixel ratio of 0.20 should provide good results.
Patch size
During training, training data is split into smaller 2D data patches, which is defined by the 'Patch size' parameter.
For example, if you choose a patch size of 64, the dataset will be cut into sub-sections of 64 x 64 pixels. These subsections will then be used as the training dataset. By subdividing images, each pass or 'epoch' should be faster and use less memory.
Batch size
Patches are randomly processed in batches and the 'Batch size' parameter determines the number of patches in a batch.
Epochs number
A single pass over all the data patches is called epoch, and the number of epochs is controlled by the 'Epochs number' parameter.
Callbacks Box
Callbacks are functions called during the training process, usually at the end of a training epoch or at the end of batch processing, that help optimize the training process. The 'Early stopping' callback, as shown below, is supported for training Noise2Void models.
Callbacks box
Although callbacks are often beneficial, they might cause undesired consequences when used improperly. For example, Early stopping might stop a training process too early, while a better solution could have been found if the training process would have been allowed to continue.
The Early Stopping callback can be set to stop training when a monitored quantity reaches a specific value, or if the results do not improve after a specific number of epochs. This can help prevent overfitting. A good guideline when using early stopping is to choose a patience level that is coherent with the selected number of epochs.
You should note the following whenever you edit the 'Set patience' setting:
With the 'As a fixed value' option checked, the computation section will be disabled and the behavior will be 'normal' and the 'patience' value in the table will be applied
With the 'Using the following computation' option checked, the 'patience' value in table will not be editable, but will be updated with the calculation result.
Early stopping parameters
Description
monitor
Lets you choose the quantity to be monitored, for example, val_loss or loss.
patience
Is the number of epochs with no improvement after which training will be stopped.
min_delta
Is the minimum change in the monitored quantity to qualify as an improvement. An absolute change of less than min_delta, will count as no improvement.
baseline
Is the baseline value for the monitored quantity to reach. Training will stop if the model doesn't show improvement over the baseline.
Learning Rate Scheduler Box
The learning rate scheduler, shown below, can be set to dynamically adjust the learning rate of a selected optimizer to help accelerate convergence during the training process. Instead of using a fixed learning rate throughout training, which can lead to suboptimal convergence or slow training, schedulers modify the learning rate based on predefined rules or the model's performance.
Learning rate scheduler box
Refer to the topic Learning Rate Scheduler for information about selecting a learning rate scheduler and setting its parameters.

documents.path: Artificial Intelligence/Custom Deep Model Architectures/Denoising with Noise2Void/Training Noise2Void Models.htm
documents.title: Training Noise2Void Models
documents.text:
Training Noise2Void Models
As an alternative to classic deep models for denoising, such as noise-to-low noise and noise-to-noise, Dragonfly provides an approach known as Noise2Void (N2V), in which training is done directly on the data to be denoised. The advantages of N2V denoising include the following:
Other classic deep-learning models for denoising, such as noise-to-low noise and noise-to-noise, may not be usable if the required outputs cannot be acquired. For Noise2Void models, each pixel is replaced with another pixel in the same image.
Training N2V models usually does not require many epochs.
N2V models are very good for reducing salt and pepper noise.
In some cases N2V may not outperform other methods that have more training information. For example, denoising performance may drop if structured noise is present.
Refer to Alexander Krull, Tim-Oliver Buchholz, Florian Jug: Noise2Void - Learning Denoising from Single Noisy Images. 2018 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.10980) for additional information about Noise2Void denoising.
Prerequisites
The following items are required for training a Noise2Void model:
Training data, which includes an input image(s) of the data you want to denoise.
The following items are optional for training a Noise2Void model:
An ROI mask, for defining the working space for the model (see Applying Masks).
A visual feedback region for monitoring the progress of training (see Enabling Visual Feedback).
Enabled the checkpoint cache. If enabled, you can load a model and then save it at a selected checkpoint after training is completed (see Saving and Loading Model Checkpoints).
Generating Noise2Void Models
Refer to the following instructions to learn how to generate Noise2Void models.
How to Generate a Noise2Void Model
Choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architectures > Noise2Void on the menu bar.
The Noise2Void dialog appears.
Click the New button on the Train tab.
The Model Information dialog appears.
Enter a name and description for the new model, as required.
Edit the default Initial filter count, if required.
Note This parameter determines the filter count at the first convolution layer.
Edit the default Depth level, if required.
Note This parameter determines the depth of the network, as determined by the number of pooling layers.
Click OK.
After processing is complete, the new model appears in the Model list.
Continue to the topic Training Models to learn how to train your new model for denoising.
Training Models
You can start training a Noise2Void model for denoising after you have generated or loaded a N2Vmodel. You should also prepare any required masks and a region for visual feedback, optional (see Prerequisites).
The initial set of training parameters should work well in most cases. You should also note that the training parameters and weights are saved with each model and can be reused for future training.
How to Train a Model
Open the Noise2Void dialog, if it is not already onscreen.
To open the dialog, choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architectures > Noise2Void on the menu bar.
Do one of the following, as required:
Generate a new Noise2Void model (see Generating Noise2Void Models).
Select an untrained or trained model from the Model list.
Note In this case, you will need to click the Load button to load the selected model.
Do the following in the Inputs box for each set of training data that you want to train the model with:
Choose your training dataset(s) in the Input drop-down menu.
Choose a mask in the Mask drop-down menu, optional.
Note If you are training with multiple training sets, click the Add New button and then choose the required input(s) and mask for the additional item(s).
The completed Inputs should look something like this:
Note You can normalize the input(s) prior to training, if required (see Normalizing Data Ranges Prior to Training or Inference).
Select and adjust the Data augmentation settings, as required (see Data Augmentation Settings).
Note In many cases, training Noise2Void models without data augmentation should provide good results.
Adjust the Training parameters, as required (see Training Parameters Tab).
Note You should monitor the estimated memory ratio when you choose the training parameter settings. The ratio should not exceed 1.00 (see Estimated Memory Ratio).
Select a region for visual feedback, optional (see Enabling Visual Feedback).
With the Visual Feedback option selected, the model’s inference will be displayed in the Training dialog in real time as each epoch is completed.
Note You can create a checkpoint cache to save copies of the model at different epochs and then load a saved checkpoint (see Saving and Loading Model Checkpoints).
Click the Train button.
The dataset is validated and then automatically split into training and validation sets before training begins. You can monitor the progress of training in the Training Model dialog, as shown below.
During training, the quantities 'loss' and 'val_loss' should decrease. You should continue to train until 'val_loss' stops decreasing.
Note You can also click the List tab and then view the training metric values for each epoch.
Wait for training the completed. You can also stop training at anytime, if required.
Evaluate the results for the training session, recommended (see Evaluating Training Results).
Preview the results of applying the trained model to the input dataset or to the source high-noise dataset to evaluate the model, recommended (see Previewing Training Results).
Note The measure of good denoising is how well detail is preserved while noise is removed.
If the results are not satisfactory, you should consider doing one or more of the following and then retraining the model:
Add an additional training set.
Create a mask centered on problematic areas (see Creating Mask ROIs).
Adjust the data augmentation settings (see Data Augmentation Settings).
Adjust the training parameter settings (see Training Parameters Tab).
When the model is trained satisfactorily, click the Save button to save your model.
Apply the model to the original dataset or to similar datasets (see Applying Noise2Void Models), as required.
Previewing Training Results
You can preview the results of training on a selected dataset with the options in the Preview box, shown below.
Preview
How to Generate a Preview
Display the required dataset.
Zoom the view, if required (see Using the Manipulate Tools).
You should note that only the section of the dataset that is visible in the view will be processed.
Select the dataset that you want the model to be applied to in the drop-down menu.
Click the Apply button.
The preview appears in the selected view.

documents.path: Artificial Intelligence/Custom Deep Model Architectures/Object Detection with YOLOv7/Applying Object Detection Models.htm
documents.title: Applying Object Detection Models
documents.text:
Applying Object Detection Models
You can automatically segment datasets with any of the object detection models that you trained, imported, or downloaded (see Training YOLOv7 Models for Object Detection for information about training an object detection model).
The following options are available for applying trained object detection models on the Apply panel in the YOLOv7 dialog (see Apply Tab).
Apply options
Description
Model
Lets you choose the required model.
Note See Model Box for additional information about filtering and other options for listed models.
Parameters
Lets you choose the input dataset and other parameters for applying the selected model.
Score… Represents the level of certainty of the model that the box contains an object of interest. Reducing this number will increase the number of boxes generated, although some boxes might be false positives. Increasing the score will decrease the number of boxes that will be detected.
IOU… The IOU (Intersection Over Union) is a parameter that regroups boxes that are superposed. Decreasing the IOU regroups more boxes and leads to less boxes.
Apply
Lets you choose how to apply the selected model. The resulting multi-ROI will added to the Data Properties and Settings panel when processing is complete.
Full Dataset… The full dataset will be processed.
Marked Slices… Only marked slices will be processed (see Marking Slices and Modifying Image Stacks).
With ROI as Mask… Only data that intersects with the labeled voxels within the selected region of interest will be processed (see Creating Mask ROIs).
With Shape as Mask… Only data that intersects with the selected shape will be processed (see Shapes Panel).
How to Apply an Object Detection Model
Choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architecture > YOLOv7 on the menu bar.
The YOLOv7 dialog appears. All of the trained models appear in the Model list on the Apply tab.
Filter the model list by entering key words in the Filter edit box, if required.
Select the model that you want to use.
The items in the Parameters box are activated.
Choose the dataset that you want to apply the model to in the Input drop-down menu.
Modify the default Score and/or IOU settings, if required.
Refer to the table Apply options for information about 'Score' and 'IOU'.
Click the Apply button and then choose how you want to apply the model, as shown below.
Note If chose to apply the model with a mask, you will need to choose a mask in the Choose an ROI as Mask dialog, as shown below, or in the Choose a Shape as Mask dialog.
The selected model is loaded and then applied. When processing is complete, a new multi-ROI appears in the Data Properties and Settings panel.

documents.path: Artificial Intelligence/Custom Deep Model Architectures/Object Detection with YOLOv7/Object Detection with YOLOv7.htm
documents.title: Object Detection with YOLOv7
documents.text:
Object Detection with YOLOv7
Object detection is a task that involves identifying the presence, location, and type of one or more objects in a given dataset, and builds upon methods for object recognition, localization, and classification.
One of the notable deep learning techniques for achieving state-of-the-art results for object detection is the 'You Only Look Once' (YOLO) family of convolutional neural networks. The YOLO family of models is a series of end-to-end deep models designed for fast object detection, that were first developed by Joseph Redmon, et al., and described in You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection.
In This Section
YOLOv7 Interface
Training YOLOv7 Models for Object Detection
Applying Object Detection Models

documents.title: Training YOLOv7 Models for Object Detection
documents.text:
Training YOLOv7 Models for Object Detection
The YOLOv7 model, which uses pre-trained weights for standard object detection problems, is accessible from the menu item Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architecture > YOLOv7. This feature simplifies the training process and lets you apply trained models on selected datasets. The results of applying a YOLOv7 object detection model are a series of 2D boxes around the objects of interest, as shown below.
From left to right: detected kidneys, yeast cells, drosophila brain
Publications
The following publications provide additional information about YOLOv7.
Joseph Redmon et al., 2016. You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection, arXiv:1506.02640 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02640)
Chien-Yao Wang et al., 2022. YOLOv7: Trainable bag-of-freebies sets new state-of-the-art for real-time object detectors, arXiv 2207.02696 (https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2207.02696).
Prerequisites
The following items are required for training YOLOv7 for object detection:
Training dataset(s) for the input. See Cropping Datasets for information about extracting a training dataset as a subset of the original data.
A target for the output, which must be a multi-ROI (see Labeling Multi-ROIs for Object Detection).
For best results, the slice size of the training set should be equal to or be a factor of the available patch sizes. If required, you can add padding (see Dataset Padding) to the training set to match an available patch size or crop (see Cropping Datasets) the input(s) to an available patch size.
The following items are optional for training YOLOv7:
An ROI mask(s), for defining the working space for the model. For example, if you want to exclude some labeled areas from the training, then you would need a mask.
Note Refer to the topic Creating Mask ROIs for information about creating mask ROIs.
Labeling Multi-ROIs for Object Detection
Multi-ROIs that are used as the target output for object detection must meet the following conditions:
The multi-ROI must have the same geometry as the input training data.
All voxels contained within the input patches must be labeled to be considered during training and each instance of an object needs to be labeled. Patches that are not fully segmented will be ignored.
Note Applying a mask may limit the number of input patches that are processed.
Label 1 must contain a fully labeled background. Other labels must contain the object classes to detect. For example, the multi-ROI for a kidney detection model may contain classes for the background and the right and left kidneys.
You should note that object detection models require boxes as an input. Dragonfly automatically internally converts each multi-ROI island into a box so that both segmentations shown below are valid training outputs. You should also note that the background is fully labeled.
Segmentation options for object detection
You can use any of the segmentation tools available on the ROI Painter and ROI Tools panels to label the voxels of a multi-ROI (see ROI Painter and ROI Tools).
Generating New YOLOv7 Models
Class count, patch size, and the input format can be selected in the Model Information dialog whenever you generate a new YOLOv7 model.
Click the New button on the Train tab to open the Model Information dialog, shown below.
Model Information dialog
The following parameters can be set in the Model Information dialog for YOLOv7 models.
Model parameters
Description
Model name
Lets you enter a name for the generated model.
Description
Lets you enter a description of your model.
Class count
Lets you enter the number of classes required for training, which must be equal to the number of labeled classes in the output multi-ROI. For example, a kidney detection model usually has three classes — 'Background', 'Left Kidney', and'Right Kidney'.
Patch size
Lets you choose a 'patch' size for training. For example, if you choose a Patch size of 256, the training data will be split into sub-sections of 256 ˣ 256 pixels. These subsections will then be used for training. By subdividing images, each pass or 'epoch' should be faster and use less memory.
Important For best results, the slice size of the training set should be equal to or be a factor of the available patch sizes. If required, you can add padding (see Dataset Padding) to the training set to match an available patch size or crop (see Cropping Datasets) the input(s) to an available patch size.
Input format
Lets you choose an input format — Grayscale or RGB.
Whenever you choose RBG as the Input format, you will need to select the red, green, and blue input channels for model training, as shown below.
How to Generate a New YOLOv7 Model
Choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architectures > YOLOv7 on the menu bar.
The YOLOv7 dialog appears.
Click the New button on the Train tab.
The Model Information dialog appears.
Enter a name and description for the new model, as required.
Choose the required Class count, as shown below.
Note The entered Class count must be equal to the number of labeled classes in the output multi-ROI.
Choose the required Patch size in the drop-down menu, as shown below.
Recommendation For best results, the slice size of the training set should be equal to or be a factor of the available patch sizes. If required, you can add padding (see Dataset Padding) to the training set to match an available patch size or crop (see Cropping Datasets) the input(s) to an available patch sizes.
Choose the Input format, as shown below.
Click OK.
After processing is complete, the model appears in the Model list and the selected number of classes appears in the Classes box, as shown below.
Continue to the topic Training YOLOv7 Models for Object Detection to learn how to train your new model.
Training YOLOv7 Models for Object Detection
You can start training a YOLOv7 model for object detection after you have prepared your training input(s) and output(s), as well as any required masks (see Prerequisites).
The initial set of training parameters should work well in most cases. You should also note that the training parameters and weights are saved with each model and can be reused for future training.
How to Train a YOLOv7 Model for Object Detection
Open the YOLOv7 dialog, if it is not already onscreen.
To open the dialog, choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architecture > YOLOv7 on the menu bar.
Do one of the following, as required:
Generate a new model for object detection (see Generating New YOLOv7 Models).
Select an untrained or trained model from the Model list that contains the required number of classes and inputs.
Rename the classes and/or assign new colors to the classes, optional.
Do the following in the Inputs box for each training set you want to train the model with:
Choose your training dataset in the Input drop-down menu.
Note If your model requires multiple inputs, for example when working with color images, select the additional input(s), as required.
Choose the labeled multi-ROI in the Output drop-down menu.
Note Only multi-ROIs with the number of classes corresponding to model's class count and that have the same geometry as the input dataset will be available in the menu.
Choose a mask in the Mask drop-down menu, optional.
Note If you are training with multiple training sets, click the Add New button and then choose the required input(s), output, and mask for the additional item(s).
The completed Inputs should look something like this:
Adjust the Data augmentation settings, as required (see Data Augmentation Settings).
Note Disabling data augmentation may result in improved performance.
Adjust the Training parameters, as required (see Training Parameters Tab).
Note You should monitor the estimated memory ratio when you choose the training parameter settings. The ratio should not exceed 1.00 (see Train Panel).
Click the Train button.
The dataset is validated and then automatically split into training and validation sets before training begins. You can monitor the progress of training in the Training Model dialog, as shown below.
During training, the quantities 'loss' and 'val_loss' should decrease. You should continue to train until 'val_loss' stops decreasing.
Note You can also click the List tab and then view the training metric values for each epoch.
Wait for training the completed. You can also stop training at anytime, if required.
Evaluate the results for the training session, recommended (see Evaluating Training Results).
Generate previews of the test set to evaluate the model, recommended (see Previewing Training Results).
If the results are not satisfactory, you should consider doing one or more of the following and then retraining the model:
Add an additional training set.
Create a mask centered on problematic areas (see Creating Mask ROIs).
Remove or adjust the data augmentation settings (see Data Augmentation Settings).
Adjust the training parameter settings (see Training Parameters Tab).
When the model is trained satisfactorily, click the Save button to save your object detection model.
Apply the model to the original dataset or to similar datasets (see Applying Object Detection Models), as required.
Previewing Training Results
You can preview the results of training on an image slice of a selected dataset with the options in the Preview box, shown below.
Preview
How to Generate a Preview
Choose to show or hide a class by changing the visibility of a class in the Classes box, optional.
Select the dataset that you want the model to be applied to in the drop-down menu.
Click the Apply button.
The preview appears in the selected view.

documents.title: YOLOv7 Interface
documents.text:
YOLOv7 Interface
The YOLOv7 dialog contains of a number of tabs and panels — Apply and Train — that you let you configure and complete a model training workflow, as well as apply a trained YOLOv7 model to selected datasets.
Choose Artificial Intelligence > Custom Deep Model Architectures > YOLOv7 on the menu bar to open the YOLOv7 dialog, shown below.
YOLOv7 dialog
Apply Tab
You can apply a trained model to detect objects on a selected dataset on the Apply tab, shown below.
A. Model boxB. Parameters box C. Apply
Model Box
The following options are available in the Model box on the Apply tab:
You can filter the models in the list by entering keywords in the Filter edit box.
You can right-click a model and then choose Open Model Folder in File Browser to open the model folder.
You can right click a model and then choose Display Training Metrics to view the training results of any training session.
Parameters Box
The options available in the Parameters box — Input, Score, and IOU — let you choose the parameters that will be applied with the selected model. Refer to the topic Applying Object Detection Models for information about applying a trained model to detect objects in a selected dataset.
Apply
Once the input selection is done, the model can be applied on the full dataset, marked slices, or with a region of interest or shape as a mask. Refer to the topic Applying Object Detection Models for information about applying a trained model to detect objects in a selected dataset.
Train Panel
The tabs on the Train panel — Models, Inputs, and Training Parameters — provide the controls and settings that let you generate and train models for object detection (see Training YOLOv7 Models for Object Detection). You should note that most of the functionalities such as input options, data augmentation, and training parameters, are the same as those for the Deep Learning Tool.
Tabs on the Train panel
Each tab on the Train panel includes an estimate of memory needed to train the model, as well as options to generate a one-slice preview of a selected model's inference (see Previewing Training Results) and to initiate training (see Training YOLOv7 Models for Object Detection).
Estimated Memory Ratio
Each tab on the Train panel displays an estimated memory ratio, which is calculated as the ratio of your system's capability and the estimated memory needed to train the model at the current over the available GPU memory. You should note that the memory needed to train a deep model is dependent on the depth of the model, as well as the selected patch and/or batch sizes.
Green … The estimated memory requirements are within your system's capabilities, typically less than 0.90.
Yellow … The estimated memory requirements are approaching your system's capabilities. Ratios between 0.90 and 1.00 may or may not result in successful training. You can adjust the batch and/or patch size to reduce the estimated memory requirement.
Red … The estimated memory requirements exceed your system's capabilities. Training often fails when ratios are greater than 1.0. You should consider adjusting the model training parameters, such as the batch and/or patch size, or selecting a shallower model, if possible.
Models Tab
The Models tab, shown below, includes controls to create new models, as well as to set the visibility and highlight colors of the labeled classes.
A. Model box B. Classes box
Model Box
You can create new models in the Model box on the Models tab, as well as duplicate and delete models.
Model box
The following options are available in the Model box on the Models tab on the Train panel:
Model settings and controls
Description
Filter
Lets you filter the model list by Model Name key words. You can also sort the list in ascending or descending order.
Model Name and Date
Indicates the name assigned to models, as well as the data and time that they were create.
Note You can edit the name of a model by double-clicking, as well right-click to open the folder in which the model was saved and to view its training history.
New
Lets you create a new model for object detection (see Generating New YOLOv7 Models).
Duplicate
Creates a copy of the selected model.
Note The name of a duplicated model can be edited by double-clicking it in the Model Name column.
Delete
Deletes the selected model.
Classes Box
The items in the Classes box correspond to the number of classes selected in the Model Information dialog when the selected model was generated. You can rename the classes, apply new colors, and choose to show or hide any of the classes when creating previews.
Classes box
Inputs Tab
The Inputs tab on the Train panel, shown below, includes an Inputs box for choosing training sets and data augmentation settings for generating addition training data.
A. Inputs box B. Data augmentation settings
Inputs Box
You can choose the input(s), output(s), and mask(s) for defining the model's working space in the Inputs box, shown below.
Inputs box
The following settings and options are available in the Inputs box.
Inputs box settings and options
Description
Dataset list
-
Lists all of the training sets selected for model training. Items include the following:
Input… Lets you select the input(s) for training the model. You can choose multiple inputs for the training input. For example, when you are working with color images.
Output… Lets you select a target output for training, which must be a multi-ROI (see Labeling Multi-ROIs for Object Detection).
Mask… Lets you select a mask to define the working space for the model, which can help reduce training times and increase training accuracy. You should note that masks should be large enough to enclose the selected Patch size and that rectangular shapes are often best (see Applying Masks).
The starting point of the input (patch) grid is calculated from the minimum (0,0) of each connected component in the mask. You should note input (patches) that do not correspond 100% with the applied mask will be ignored during training. You should also note that patches that correspond to the applied mask, but that are not fully segmented, will be ignored during training. For example, in cases in which the background (class 1) is not labeled.
Edit Calibration
Opens the Normalization dialog, in which you can normalize calibrated and uncalibrated datasets prior to training (see Normalizing Data Ranges Prior to Training or Inference).
Add
Adds a new item to the datasets list. The input(s) and output for the item can be selected in the respective drop-down menus.
Remove
Removes the selected item from the datasets list.
Export as AI
Saves all training data inputs, outputs, and masks as slices in the native Dragonfly (*.ORSObject extension) file format. Saving only data that is used for training can significantly reduce the size of training sets.
Import as AI
Imports all training data that was exported as AI. All saved inputs, outputs, and masks for each training set will be added to the dialog when the data is imported, minimizing any additional manual entry.
Data Augmentation Settings
The performance of neural networks often improves with the amount of data available, particularly the ability of the fit models to generalize what they have learned to new images.
However, disabling data augmentation for training a YOLOv7 model for object detection may also result in improved performance.
You should consider experimenting with the different data augmentation methods to determine which ones result in a measurable improvement to model performance.
Check the Generate additional training data by augmentation option to activate the Data augmentation settings, shown below.
Data augmentation settings
Refer to the topic Data Augmentation Settings for more information about the Data augmentation settings.
Training Parameters Tab
The basic settings that you need to set to train a YOLOv7 model are available in the Training parameters box, as shown below, on the Training Parameters tab.
Training parameters box
The training parameters are a stripped down version of those found in the Deep Learning Tool. In most cases, the default values should give good results.
Training parameters
Description
Learning rate
Learning rate is a hyper-parameter that controls the weights of neural network with respect to the loss gradient. It defines how quickly the neural network updates the concepts it has learned.
A desirable learning rate is low enough that the network converges to something useful, but high enough that it can be trained in a reasonable amount of time. A small learning rate makes the model converge slowly to the global minimum loss.
Note The default learning rate of 0.001 works way better than the usual rate for other deep models, which is set by default at 1.0.
Validation percentage
Lets you choose the percentage of the training data that will be used for validation. In this case, the training set will be used for training and the validation set will be used only for accuracy evaluation, but not for training.
Batch size
Patches are randomly processed in batches and the 'Batch size' parameter determines the number of patches in a batch.
Epochs number
A single pass over all the data patches is called epoch, and the number of epochs is controlled by the 'Epochs Number' parameter.

documents.title: Applying Deep Models
documents.text:
Applying Deep Models
You can apply deep models trained for semantic segmentation and regression tasks to selected datasets with the options in the Apply box, shown below. You should note that the Apply options are available on the Model Training and Model Overview panels of the Deep Learning tool. You can apply models to the full dataset, marked slices, or within a mask.
Apply options
How Images are Tiled During Inference
When a trained model is applied to a dataset, Dragonfly automatically divides the input volume into patches and passes each patch through the network to produce 'per-voxel' class probabilities. The voxel is then assigned to the class with the highest probability. The tiling strategy depends on the model's input dimension:
3D models (e.g., U-Net 3D)… The same fixed cubic patch size that was used during training is also used during inference.
2D and 2.5D models… Dragonfly dynamically selects the largest 2D patch size that fits in the available GPU memory at the time of inference. This maximizes throughput and minimizes patch-boundary blending artefacts in the in-plane directions.
The stride ratio is a training-only parameter that controls how labeled patches are sampled from training data. It does not apply at inference time. Dragonfly handles the internal stitching of patch predictions automatically to produce a seamless, full-resolution output over the entire dataset.
You can also apply deep models trained for semantic segmentation to your image data in the Segment with AI panel (see Segment with AI). Denoising and super-resolution models can be applied to your image data in the Filter with AI panel (see Filter with AI).
How to Apply a Deep Model
Select the required trained model on the Model Overview panel, if required.
Generate a preview to verify the loaded model, recommended (see Previewing Model Inference).
Select the required input(s) in the Input drop-down menu.
If your model has an input dimension of 2.5D or 3D, select a reference slice and spacing. These options are circled below.
If required, you can normalize the data range prior to applying the model (see Normalizing Data Ranges Prior to Training or Inference).
Click the Apply button and then choose an option in the drop-down menu, as described below.
Full Dataset… The full dataset will be segmented. In this case, processing will start automatically.
Marked Slices… Only marked slices will be segmented (see Marking Image Slices). In this case, processing will start automatically.
With ROI as Mask… Only data within the region of interest selected as the mask will be processed (see Creating Mask ROIs). You can choose the required mask in the Choose an ROI as Mask dialog and then click OK to start processing.
With Shape as Mask… If selected, only data within the shape selected as the mask will be processed (see Shapes). You can choose the required mask in the Choose a Shape as Mask dialog and then click OK to start processing.
When processing is complete, a new multi-ROI or processed dataset is added to the Data Properties and Settings panel.
